maria: Quick q: setting up REDWOOD_API_KEY in Node + curl — our SDK accepts Basic auth but docs show Bearer. When should I use Basic vs Bearer? Seeing 401s when I set env var in .env.

alex: Basic is used when you pass the key as username with empty password (some libs). Bearer is simpler if SDK supports it. 401s usually env quoting or newline issues.

maria: Example I'm doing: Authorization: Basic <base64>. But I tried Buffer.from(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY).toString('base64') and it failed.

noah: You must include trailing colon in the string before base64. It's base64(api_key + ':'). So Buffer.from(KEY + ':').toString('base64'). Without colon auth server sees no password field and rejects.

maria: ah! so Buffer.from(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY + ':').toString('base64') — got it. For curl I used -u "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" (no colon) — does that work?

alex: curl -u accepts username:password; if you pass only username it prompts for password or treats as empty? Use -u "$REDWOOD_API_KEY:" (note colon). Example:
```
curl -u "$REDWOOD_API_KEY:" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

sam: Also watch out for dotenv. If your .env has REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk_..." the quotes get included depending on parser. Recommended: REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_xxx (no quotes) or use dotenv-safe. On Windows PowerShell use $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY='sk...' (single quotes to avoid interpolation).

devx-bot: Docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/auth — examples for Node/Python/curl. :link:

noah: Node example:
```
headers: {
  'Authorization': `Basic ${Buffer.from(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY + ':').toString('base64')}`
}
```
or better yet if SDK exposes client that accepts apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY. Python:
```
import os, requests
resp = requests.get(url, auth=(os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'], ''))
```

maria: Thanks — saved me. One more: what if API key contains colon? base64 will handle it but server splits auth on first colon so embedded colons in username are allowed? Should be fine since it's encoded; server decodes then splits at first colon — if key contains colon it will be ambiguous. But API keys shouldn't contain colon. If they do contact support.

alex: Short answer: keys should avoid colon; if they do, use Bearer or pass via SDK. Also make sure no trailing newline in env — `cat .env | xargs` to verify.

maria: :thumbsup: will switch to REDWOOD_API_KEY: in env and test. thanks all.
